What Are Immediate Load Dental Implants?

Immediate load dental implants refer to an approach where a temporary crown or restoration is attached to the implant shortly after it has been placed, rather than waiting for the full healing period before any restoration is fitted. This means that, in suitable cases, patients may leave their appointment with a temporary tooth in place on the same day as implant placement.

The key requirement for immediate loading is that the implant achieves sufficient primary stability at the time of placement. This stability depends on the quality and volume of the bone at the implant site. Your clinician will assess these factors during your consultation and at the time of the procedure to determine whether immediate loading is clinically appropriate.

It is important to understand that the temporary restoration placed during immediate loading serves as a provisional tooth while the implant heals and integrates with the bone. A permanent crown is fitted at a later stage once healing has been confirmed.

Who May Be Suitable for Immediate Load Implants?

Immediate loading is not appropriate for every patient. Suitability is assessed on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the clinical conditions at the implant site and the patient's overall oral health. Factors that may support suitability include:

  • Patients with a single missing tooth or a small number of missing teeth where bone conditions are favourable
  • Sufficient bone volume and density at the implant site to achieve strong primary stability
  • Adequate implant stability confirmed at the time of placement
  • Good overall oral health with no active infection at the treatment site
  • Patients who would benefit from beginning the restoration process sooner

If you are dealing with missing teeth and are interested in immediate loading, a clinical assessment will confirm whether this approach is suitable for your individual case.

Important Information

Not all patients are suitable for immediate loading. In some cases, the conventional approach — where the implant is left to heal before a restoration is attached — may be more clinically appropriate.

Factors such as bone quality, the location of the implant, overall health, and habits such as clenching or grinding may influence whether immediate loading is recommended.

Your clinician will discuss all available options with you and recommend the approach that best suits your clinical circumstances.

Benefits of Immediate Load Implants

Where immediate loading is clinically appropriate, the approach may offer certain advantages compared to the conventional pathway. These potential benefits depend on the individual case and clinical findings.

Restoring Appearance Sooner

A temporary restoration is attached shortly after implant placement, which may help restore the appearance of the smile sooner than the conventional approach where a gap remains during the healing period.

Beginning Restoration Quickly

The restoration process begins on the same day as implant placement, meaning the treatment moves forward without the waiting period typically associated with conventional implant restoration.

Reducing Time Without a Visible Tooth

For patients concerned about being without a visible tooth, immediate loading may offer a way to minimise the time spent with a gap in the smile, depending on suitability and clinical conditions.

The benefits of immediate loading depend on individual clinical factors. Your clinician will discuss what you can realistically expect based on your specific case.

The Immediate Load Implant Treatment Process

Immediate load implant treatment is carried out in carefully managed stages. Your clinician will guide you through each step and ensure you are fully informed throughout the process.

01

Consultation and Examination

Your treatment begins with a comprehensive consultation. Your clinician examines the treatment site, discusses your goals, and assesses whether immediate loading may be a suitable approach for your case.

02

Clinical Assessment of Bone and Tooth Condition

A detailed assessment of the bone quality, volume, and the condition of the surrounding teeth and gums is carried out. This evaluation is essential for determining whether the implant site can support immediate loading.

03

Implant Placement

The dental implant is placed at the prepared site under local anaesthetic. During placement, your clinician assesses the primary stability of the implant to confirm whether immediate loading can proceed as planned.

04

Temporary Restoration Where Clinically Appropriate

If sufficient stability is confirmed, a temporary crown or restoration is attached to the implant. This provisional restoration serves as a functional and aesthetic placeholder while the implant integrates with the surrounding bone over the healing period.

05

Final Crown After Healing

Once the healing period is complete and the implant has successfully integrated, the temporary restoration is replaced with a permanent crown. The final crown is designed to match the shape, shade, and function of your natural teeth.

Treatment timelines vary depending on individual clinical circumstances. Your clinician will provide a clear outline of the expected process during your consultation. Learn more about dental implants and how they work.

Immediate Load vs Traditional Implant Restoration

The main difference between immediate loading and the traditional approach lies in when the restoration is attached to the implant. Understanding both options can help you discuss the most appropriate approach with your clinician.

Key differences include:

  • Immediate loading — a temporary restoration is attached shortly after implant placement, provided sufficient stability is achieved
  • Traditional (delayed) loading — the implant is left to heal and integrate with the bone before any restoration is attached, typically over a period of several months
  • Implant stability is the primary factor in determining which approach is appropriate — immediate loading requires strong primary stability at placement
  • Both approaches aim for the same long-term outcome: a stable, well-integrated implant supporting a permanent restoration
  • Treatment planning considerations, including bone quality and the location of the implant, influence which method your clinician recommends

Your clinician will explain the advantages and considerations of each approach during your consultation. For patients interested in full-arch restoration with early loading, our same day dental implants page provides further information on that treatment pathway.

Immediate Load Dental Implants Cost in London

The cost of immediate load dental implants in London varies depending on the individual case. Because each treatment plan is developed following a clinical assessment, it is not possible to provide a fixed price without first evaluating your specific needs.

Factors that may influence the cost include:

  • The number of implants required
  • The type of temporary and permanent restoration planned
  • The complexity of the case and any preparatory treatment needed
  • The condition of the bone and surrounding structures
  • The overall treatment plan and number of stages involved

We recommend attending a consultation to receive a personalised assessment and a detailed quotation that reflects the scope of your treatment. Finance options may be available to help manage the cost, subject to status.
